sentences.show: In 1864, 109 Union officers escaped from a Confederate prison, through a tunnel dug in a cellar full of rats.
Libby Prison, in Richmond, Virginia. An old warehouse, packed with captured Union officers.
The guards thought it was escape-proof. They even painted the walls white, so anyone sneaking outside would stand out.
But in the basement was a room nobody wanted to enter. Flooded, pitch dark, and crawling with rats. They called it Rat Hell.
Colonel Thomas Rose and his men got in through a chimney, behind a stove.
Every night they dug, with almost no tools, while hundreds of rats ran over them.
The dirt went under the straw. One man stayed buried in it all day, to hide the hole.
After 17 days, the tunnel came up under a tobacco shed, outside the prison.
On the night of 9 February, they simply walked out into the streets of Richmond. Rose strolled right past a sentry.
Then the whole prison found out, and stampeded for the hole. A guard heard the racket, and joked that somebody's coffeepot had tipped over.
109 men got out. Nobody noticed for almost twelve hours.
Following the North Star, 59 of them reached Union lines.
Their leader wasn't one of them. Rose was caught minutes from the Union front, and dragged back to Libby.
So, would you have crawled into Rat Hell?
They followed the North Star. Follow the channel, and subscribe.
